title.en: Death and the art that survives

heading.en: What remains after we are gone?

hook.en: Long after a painter dies, her paintings can still hang on walls. The last part of the poem asks what will remain of Aunt Jennifer.

objectives.en: Interpret the final stanza of the poem
Explain the phrase about ordeals she was mastered by
Understand art's power to outlive the artist

narration.en: Long after a painter dies, her paintings can still hang on walls. The last part of the poem asks what will remain of Aunt Jennifer.

body.en: The poet imagines Aunt Jennifer after her death: her terrified hands will lie still, yet still ringed with the ordeals that mastered her. Even death does not free her from the marks of her suffering. The word ringed recalls the wedding band and the lifelong bondage it brought.

points.en: After death, her hands lie still
Still ringed: marked by her ordeals
She was mastered by her trials

narration.en: The poet imagines Aunt Jennifer after her death: her terrified hands will lie still, yet still ringed with the ordeals that mastered her. Even death does not free her from the marks of her suffering. The word ringed recalls the wedding band and the lifelong bondage it brought.
Let us lay out the poem as a timeline from the tigers to after her death.

say.en: Read from top to bottom. Stanza one shows the proud tigers on the screen.
Stanza two shows her nervous fingers at work.
The heavy wedding band explains her fear.
Stanza three imagines her death, still marked by her ordeals.
But the tigers she made go on prancing, proud and unafraid.

body.en: While Aunt Jennifer remains defeated even in death, the tigers she created will go on prancing, proud and unafraid. Her art outlives her and keeps alive the spirit of freedom she could never express. This shows the lasting power of art as a voice for the silenced.

heading.en: Ringed for life, ringed in death

body.en: Link the ring to the word ringed: the wedding ring binds her in life, and she is still ringed with ordeals in death. Only the tigers break free.

mnemonic.en: Ring in life, ringed in death, tigers free

narration.en: Link the ring to the word ringed: the wedding ring binds her in life, and she is still ringed with ordeals in death. Only the tigers break free.

problem.en: Contrast Aunt Jennifer's fate with that of her tigers.

steps.en: Describe the tigers: proud, fearless and free; they will go on prancing.
Describe the aunt: nervous, burdened, and still ringed with ordeals even in death.
Explain the irony: the creator is defeated while her creation survives.
Conclude: art preserves the spirit of freedom that her life denied.

answer.en: The tigers are proud, fearless and free, and they will go on prancing after she dies. Aunt Jennifer is nervous and burdened all her life, and even in death her hands remain ringed with ordeals. Ironically, the timid creator is defeated, but her art survives, carrying the freedom she never had.
